title: Share Trading Policy
date_next_review: Maintained and reviewed by the Company Secretary and General Counsel; no cycle stated

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Each director of the Company, including the Chair of the Executive Committee (CEC), and the CEO, together with their Connected Persons. Must obtain prior written approval for any proposed dealing outside a blackout period: the Chair of the Board from the Board or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee, and any other director from the Chair of the Board.

tiers.name: senior executives
tiers.description: All direct reports to the CEO, COO and CEC. Ordinarily subject only to post-trade notification under paragraph 4.2, but must obtain paragraph 4.1 prior approval for any dealing connected with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.

tiers.name: Other Relevant Persons
tiers.description: Relevant Persons other than directors and the CEO: officers of the Group, participants in any share or option scheme offered by the Group, employees and consultants working in the Group's Sydney office, and any other key management personnel as defined in the Accounting Standards. Subject to the blackout periods and the hedging rules, with post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within 2 business days.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: Closely related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act) of Personnel. Where the Policy requires a Relevant Person to do an act or thing, such as obtaining permission, the relevant Personnel must do that act or thing in respect of his or her Connected Persons.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Company securities.

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 31 December each year (or the last trading day before that day)
windows.end_anchor: the day following the announcement to ASX of the preliminary final statement or full year results

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on 30 June each year (or the last trading day before that day)
windows.end_anchor: the day following the announcement of the half-yearly results

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on 31 March (or the last trading day before that day)
windows.end_anchor: the day following the release of the relevant quarterly report

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on 30 September (or the last trading day before that day)
windows.end_anchor: the day following the release of the relevant quarterly report

windows.start_anchor: commencement of any other period that the Board specifies from time to time

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other blackout period from time to time. Separately, where the Company is in possession of inside information it may notify Relevant Persons that they must not deal, either for a specified period or until the Company gives further notice. The Policy does not state whether such notices are confidential.

rules.detail: Hedging with financial products, which covers OTC puts and calls, is expressly permitted over vested and unrestricted Company securities. The hedge transaction is treated as a dealing, so a director or the CEO must obtain prior written approval from the Chair of the Board (or, for the Chair, from the Board or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee) and must not transact during a blackout period. The blackout ban expressly extends to financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities on the following conditions: the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications are made on this basis

rules.detail: For Relevant Persons other than directors and the CEO, the hedge is a dealing requiring only notification to the Company Secretary within 2 business days after it occurs, plus compliance with the blackout periods.
rules.evidence: Where a Relevant Person other than a director or the CEO (or his or her Connected Persons) deals in the Company's securities, the Relevant Person must notify the Company Secretary of any such dealing within 2 business days of the relevant dealing occurring.

rules.detail: Overriding prohibition: Company securities must never be hedged before vesting, and Relevant Persons are specifically barred from any hedge transaction involving unvested equity held under any employee, executive or director equity plan. No waiver route is provided for this prohibition.
rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged prior to the vesting of those Company securities. In particular, Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into any hedge transaction involving unvested equity held pursuant to any employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company

rules.detail: Vested securities that remain subject to a holding lock or a restriction on dealing under an equity plan can never be hedged, so only fully released shares are available for a collar.
rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of any employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Hedging vested and unrestricted Company securities is expressly permitted provided the transaction is treated as a dealing and the paragraph 4.1 approval or paragraph 4.2 notification requirements are satisfied. The hedge must also not be entered into, renewed, altered or closed out while the Relevant Person holds inside information, and the Company may disclose the fact and nature of the hedge.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities on the following conditions: ... the relevant requirements under paragraphs 4.1 and 4.2 of this Policy have been satisfied.

rules.detail: Absolute prohibition on hedging unvested Company securities and unvested equity plan holdings, extended to Connected Persons through the paragraph 2 procurement obligation.
rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged prior to the vesting of those Company securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar or similar structure over vested unrestricted shares is a dealing (it is a financial product issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities and an agreement to sell securities) and would generally also be a hedge under paragraph 4.4, so it needs paragraph 4.1 approval or 4.2 notification. Forward contracts are given as an example of short-term dealings, so a short-dated monetisation is caught by paragraph 3.3.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: Short selling is not named in this Policy. Relevant Persons are also subject to the Company's separate Insider Trading Policy, which is not part of this document.

Securities lending is not named and is not within the description of dealing, which extends to exercising options and to procuring and entering into agreements to subscribe for, buy or sell securities.

CFDs are not named but are transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Company securities, so they fall within the definition of hedging and are permitted over vested unrestricted holdings subject to approval or notification. An actively traded CFD position would breach the short-term trading ban in paragraph 3.3.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Company securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending is expressly permitted. Entering into the arrangement, transferring securities into an existing margin loan account and selling securities to satisfy a margin call are each dealings. Directors and senior executives (including the CEO and CEC) must obtain paragraph 4.1 approval for any such dealing irrespective of any trading window, and the Company may impose conditions on that approval.
rules.evidence: Directors and senior executives (including the CEO and CEC) must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in paragraph 4.1 for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.

rules.detail: Senior executives, who otherwise only notify after dealing, are pulled up into the director-level prior approval regime for any dealing connected with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.
rules.evidence: Directors and senior executives (including the CEO and CEC) must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in paragraph 4.1 for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.

rules.detail: Granting security is not prohibited. The only express encumbrance regime is for margin lending arrangements, where entry and the transfer of securities into the loan account are dealings requiring approval. A pledge outside a margin lending arrangement is not separately named, although paragraph 4.5(g) contemplates secured lenders generally.
rules.evidence: Any dealing in the Company's securities by Relevant Persons pursuant to a margin lending arrangement must be conducted in accordance with this Policy. Such dealings will include: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account

rules.detail: There is no ban on secured financing. The Policy regulates margin lending expressly and, subject to paragraph 4.3, excludes from the approval and blackout rules a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights. The Company may make any margin lending approval conditional, for example on the circumstances in which securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call.
rules.evidence: subject to paragraph 4.3, a disposal of securities of the Company or the securities of Yanzhou that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: The Policy does not address whether unvested equity plan holdings or securities under a holding lock may be given as collateral; paragraph 4.4 restricts only hedging of those holdings.

Relevant Persons must not deal on a short-term trading basis, which includes buying and selling on market within a 3 month period and entering into other short-term dealings, with forward contracts given as the example. No carve-outs are listed and no waiver is provided, although the paragraph 4.5 exclusions disapply paragraphs 3.2 and 4.1 to 4.4 but not paragraph 3.3.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons must not deal in the Company's securities on a short-term trading basis. Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

No loan to value ratio or trigger level is specified.

Other Relevant Persons: notification of any dealing to the Company Secretary within 2 business days of the dealing
Any Relevant Person entering a hedging arrangement: the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge, for example in its annual report or to ASX; no deadline stated

Employee, executive and director equity plans operated by the Company or Yanzhou
exemption_authority: Waiver from the blackout periods only, in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, compulsion by court order, or any other circumstance deemed exceptional by the approver, but never where the person holds inside information). Approvers are the Chair or Vice-Chair of the Board for directors, officers and senior executives including the CEO; the Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee for the Chair or Vice-Chair; the CEO for other Relevant Persons; or their delegate. The application must be in writing with sufficient evidence that the dealing is the only reasonable course of action, and any waiver granted lasts 1 business day. There is no authority to waive the paragraph 4.4(b) hedging prohibitions or the paragraph 3.3 short-term trading ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: express permission to hedge vested shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: Relevant Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities on the following conditions: the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications are made on this basis; and the relevant requirements under paragraphs 4.1 and 4.2 of this Policy have been satisfied.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an express, affirmative permission for the derivative legs of a collar over vested unrestricted shares, subject only to the ordinary approval and notification machinery - among the clearest hedging permissions on the ASX.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the hedge transaction must not be entered into, renewed, altered or closed out when the Relevant Person is in possession of inside information
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every roll, reset, amendment and unwind of the collar is separately gated, so the documentation must not require the executive to act at a fixed date that could coincide with possession of inside information.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending approval overrides trading windows
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and senior executives (including the CEO and CEC) must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in paragraph 4.1 for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for the financing leg is required at all times, but the phrase 'irrespective of any trading window' also signals that such approval can be sought and given outside an open window, which helps if the facility must be varied during a blackout.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with 4.3(b) conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company can dictate the enforcement terms of the bank's facility, for example restricting when collateral may be sold on a margin call, so the credit terms must be agreed with the issuer as well as the borrower.

bespoke_clauses.clause: subject to paragraph 4.3, a disposal of securities of the Company or the securities of Yanzhou that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from paragraphs 3.2 and 4.1 to 4.4].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Lender enforcement, including during a blackout, is carved out of the blackout and approval rules provided the paragraph 4.3 approval regime was observed, so the bank's security can be enforced without putting the executive in breach.

bespoke_clauses.topic: borrower-side margin call sales are dealings
bespoke_clauses.clause: Such dealings will include: ... selling securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A sale by the executive to meet a margin call is a dealing needing prior approval, so the facility should rely on lender-exercised rights or cash cure rather than obliging the borrower to sell.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Naming forward contracts means a short-dated collar or forward-settled leg risks characterisation as prohibited short-term trading, so tenor should comfortably exceed three months and the exclusions in paragraph 4.5 do not disapply this ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where a Relevant Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of Company securities, the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (eg in its annual report or to ASX).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The existence and nature of the collar may be publicly disclosed, so the parties should assume no confidentiality over the structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a waiver is granted, the Relevant Person will be notified in writing (which may include notification via email) and in each circumstance the duration of the waiver to deal in securities will be 1 business day.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any blackout waiver gives only a single business day to price and execute, which is impractical for negotiating a collar, so the transaction must be planned for an open period.

bespoke_clauses.topic: four blackouts a year plus Yanzhou securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Relevant Persons must not deal in the securities of the Company or Yanzhou Coal Mining Company Limited (Yanzhou) during any of the following blackout periods [31 December, 30 June, 31 March and 30 September, each until the day after the relevant results or quarterly report].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Quarterly blackouts leave relatively short open periods for entry and unwind, and the same restrictions apply to dealings in the listed parent's securities, which matters if the hedge references Yanzhou rather than Yancoal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Relevant Person must undertake the proposed dealing as soon as possible once the notification is provided or approval is granted or such other period specified in the approval. If the dealing is not undertaken within this time, the notification will no longer have effect and new notification or approval will be required.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no fixed validity period, only an 'as soon as possible' standard, so the approval should specify an express window long enough to document and settle the collar and the loan.

summary: A funded collar is workable at Yancoal over vested and unrestricted shares. Paragraph 4.4(c) expressly permits Relevant Persons to hedge vested and unrestricted Company securities, defining hedging as transactions in financial products that limit the economic risk of holding Company securities, provided the hedge is treated as a dealing and cleared under the ordinary machinery: prior written approval from the Chair of the Board for directors, the CEO and the CEC, and post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within 2 business days for everyone else. The financing leg is also available: paragraph 4.3 regulates rather than bans margin lending, requiring directors and senior executives to obtain paragraph 4.1 approval for entering the arrangement, transferring shares into the loan account or selling to meet a call, irrespective of any trading window, and the Company may attach conditions including on when shares may be sold to satisfy a margin call; a lender's enforcement disposal is then excluded from the blackout and approval rules. The hard limits are that securities must never be hedged before vesting or while subject to a holding lock or plan dealing restriction, that no hedge may be entered, renewed, altered or closed out while the person holds inside information, and that the tenor must exceed three months because paragraph 3.3 treats forward contracts as prohibited short-term dealings. Practical constraints are the four annual blackout periods around the full year, half year and two quarterly reports plus any Board-specified period, the one business day duration of any exceptional circumstances waiver, and the Company's right to disclose the fact and nature of the hedge in its annual report or to the ASX.
